SSME blades are subject to severe thermal, pressure, and forced vibration environments.
The SSME/STAEBL code was developed by systematically modifying and enhancing the STAEBL (Structural Tailoring of Engine Blades) code.

Additions and modifications to STAEBL in SSME/STAEBL include thermal stress analysis, gas dynamic (pressure) loads, temperature-dependent material and thermal properties, forced vibrations, and a direct time integration algorithm for transient dynamic response.
Optimization studies showed that the inclusion of thermal and pressure loads, in addition to centrifugal loads, requires additional weight in the optimized design to meet all constraints.
The temperature dependence of material properties, which reduces the yield stress, was a key factor in requiring the additional weight.
For the SSME blade designs dominated by root stress constraints, the crystal axis orientation was a relatively unimportant design variable compared to the geometric design variables.
Blade cross-section stacking offsets were shown to have a very significant effect on root stress-dominated SSME blade designs.
The natural frequencies of the optimized SSME blade design under centrifugal loads only increased slightly compared to the initial design.
The SSME blade weight remained essentially unchanged at 4.15 lb between the initial and optimized designs when considering centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads.
For the single-crystal SSME blade, the root stress and stage weight were relatively insensitive to the crystal orientation.
The root stress constraint was extremely sensitive to the blade stacking design variables in the SSME blade optimization.

The final optimized SSME blade design had a thickness distribution of 0.226, 0.138, 0.091 inches from root to tip, a root chord of 0.890 inches, and stacking variables of A = -0.0012, B = 0.0071, C = 0.0013, and D = 0.0095, resulting in a root stress of 72 ksi.
